_comment: Plain-language text for every Intelligence check, keyed by check code. The check's own code (ziira/modules/*/ ... IntelCheck) holds the title, limits and technical description; this file adds what a business owner needs: what it means, a made-up example, and the limits in plain words. tests/test_check_catalog.py fails if a check has no entry here, or an entry has no check. Regenerate the catalogue with `make site-catalog`.

cash.title: Cash, sales and payments
cash.lead: Is the money you should have received actually there?

cashier.title: Cashiers, discounts and the till
cashier.lead: Do the habits at the till look normal?

stock.title: Stock and shrinkage
stock.lead: Is stock going missing, running out or going to waste?

customers.title: Customers and credit
customers.lead: Who owes you, and are you lending to the wrong people?

suppliers.title: Suppliers and purchasing
suppliers.lead: Are you paying more, paying twice or paying for goods that never came?

books.title: Accounting and books
books.lead: Do the entries in your books look ordinary?

people.title: People and payroll
people.lead: Is anyone being paid in a way that looks odd?

services.title: Appointments, jobs and billable time
services.lead: Are clients turning up, jobs moving and finished work being invoiced?

controls.title: Controls and approvals
controls.lead: Is the system itself being used in a careful way?

_units.standalone: A connected system or uploaded file

_params.days: How many days back to look
_params.idle_weeks: Weeks without a visit before a member counts as gone quiet
_params.max_overrides: Refused people one person may let in before it is flagged
_params.lookback_days: How many days back to look
_params.min_sales: Fewest sales needed before a cashier is judged
_params.min_rate: Smallest share of sales worth flagging (0.05 means 5 in every 100)
_params.grace_days: Days to wait before it counts as a problem
_params.min_earlier: Fewest earlier records needed to compare with
_params.high_days_overdue: Days overdue at which it becomes high priority
_params.min_days_overdue: Days past the due date before a customer is flagged
_params.window_minutes: How many minutes apart still counts as the same event
_params.tolerance_percent: How big a difference (in %) is allowed before flagging
_params.backdate_days: How many days earlier than the entry date counts as back-dated
_params.within_days: How many days apart counts as close together
_params.window_days: How many days of history to compare
_params.value_limit: Value above which it is flagged
_params.min_days_late: Fewest days late before it is flagged
_params.high_days_late: Days late at which it becomes high priority
_params.min_history: Fewest days of history needed to know what is normal
_params.drop_percent: How far below normal (in %) counts as a big drop
_params.deviations: How many times the usual swing counts as unusual
_params.rise_percent: How big a price rise (in %) is flagged
_params.percent: Share (in %) above which it is flagged
_params.limit: Amount above which it is flagged
_params.hours: Hours to wait before it counts as a problem
_params.history_days: How many days of earlier history to compare with
_params.min_invoices: Fewest invoices needed to judge how a customer pays
_params.increase_percent: How much slower (in %) counts as slower
_params.min_increase_days: Fewest extra days to take longer to pay before flagging
_params.min_items: Fewest items before it is flagged
_params.min_quantity: Smallest number of units worth flagging
_params.min_actions: Fewest changes in a day before it is flagged
_params.min_hours: Fewest extra overtime hours worth flagging
_params.min_samples: Fewest earlier days needed to know what is normal
_params.min_ratio: How many times the usual amount counts as unusual
_params.min_margin_percent: Profit margin (in %) below which the squeeze is flagged
_params.look_back_days: How many days back to look
_params.late_days: Days past due before it is flagged
_params.min_lines: Fewest answered lines before a payer is compared
_params.times_usual: How many times more than your other payers
_params.min_repeats: How many times the same reason counts

finance.backdated_entries.plain: An entry was put into the books long after the date it carries, so the past was changed after the fact.
finance.backdated_entries.example: On 3 October someone posted an expense dated 12 July.

limits.late_days: Days between the entry date and when it was made that counts as late
limits.manual_only: Look only at hand-made entries (1 = yes, 0 = all)

finance.low_gross_margin.plain: You are keeping a smaller share of each sale than you usually do, after paying for what you sold.
finance.low_gross_margin.example: Gross margin this month is 14%, against 26% over the last three months.

limits.drop_points: How many points below normal the margin must fall
limits.min_income: Smallest sales for the month before it is judged
limits.min_day: Earliest day of the month to judge (so the first days are not read too early)

finance.period_reopened.plain: A month that was closed and locked was opened again, so numbers you already relied on can change.
finance.period_reopened.example: June was closed on 5 July and reopened on 19 July.

finance.posted_after_close.plain: Something was posted into a month after that month had been closed.
finance.posted_after_close.example: A 12,000 entry dated May appeared after May was closed.

finance.stale_reconciliation.plain: A bank reconciliation (ticking your records off against the bank statement) was started and never finished.
finance.stale_reconciliation.example: The February reconciliation of the main account has been open for 41 days.

limits.days_open: Days a reconciliation may stay open before it is flagged

finance.unreconciled_bank_lines.plain: Money that moved through a bank account is still not matched to a line on the bank statement after a long time.
finance.unreconciled_bank_lines.example: 6 entries on the main account are older than 45 days and still unmatched.

limits.age_days: Days old before an unmatched entry is flagged
limits.days: How many days back to look

finance.unusual_expense.plain: A branch spent much more on one kind of expense in a day than it normally does.
finance.unusual_expense.example: Branch B spent 8,400 on repairs on Tuesday; it usually spends about 900 in a day.

limits.min_ratio: How many times the usual daily spend counts as unusual
limits.min_samples: Days of history needed to know what is usual

standalone.expense_unusually_high.plain: One expense is much bigger than the usual expense in the same category.
standalone.expense_unusually_high.example: A 45,000 vehicle repair, when vehicle repairs usually cost 6,000.

standalone.manual_journal.plain: An entry typed into the books by hand looks worth a second look: it is large, a perfectly round figure, made at night, dated in the past, or created and approved by the same person.
standalone.manual_journal.example: A round 500,000 journal made at 23:40 and approved by the person who wrote it.

limits.large_amount: Amount above which a hand-made entry counts as large
limits.round_step: Round figures are multiples of this
limits.backdate_days: Days earlier than entry date that counts as back-dated

standalone.unmatched_receipt.plain: Money arrived (on a mobile-money or bank statement) that matches no sale and no invoice.
standalone.unmatched_receipt.example: A 12,500 receipt from last Friday that no sale or invoice accounts for.
standalone.unmatched_receipt.needs: Payments, plus sales or invoices to compare with

limits.days: How many days back to look
limits.grace_days: Days to wait before it counts as unmatched
limits.window_minutes: How many minutes apart a payment and a sale can be and still match

payments.close_variance.plain: A branch closed its day with more or less money than the records say it should have.
payments.close_variance.example: Branch A closed the day 1,350 short.

limits.variance_limit: Difference above which a close is flagged

payments.failing_prompts.plain: Many payment requests sent to customers' phones failed or timed out on the same day, which usually means a fault with the payment service.
payments.failing_prompts.example: 9 of 12 payment requests failed on Saturday.

limits.min_attempts: Fewest requests in a day before it is judged
limits.failure_percent: Share of requests that must fail (in %)

payments.settlement_mismatch.plain: What your mobile-money account received does not agree with what was paid across to your bank.
payments.settlement_mismatch.example: The account received 220,000 this week but only 205,000 reached the bank.

limits.grace_days: Days a transfer may take before it counts as missing

payments.unlinked_receipts.plain: Money was received but is not linked to any sale, invoice or customer.
payments.unlinked_receipts.example: A 3,200 payment came in on Monday and nothing explains what it was for.

limits.hours: Hours to wait before it counts as unlinked

payments.unmatched_transactions.plain: Your mobile-money provider or bank reported money coming in that none of your recorded payments accounts for.
payments.unmatched_transactions.example: The provider shows 7 receipts last week that Ziira cannot tie to any sale.

limits.unmatched_days: Days a transaction may stay unmatched before it is flagged

pos.branch_sales_low.plain: A branch sold far less than it normally sells on that day of the week.
pos.branch_sales_low.example: Branch C sold 18,000 on Saturday; a normal Saturday is about 52,000.

pos.till_cash_variance.plain: A cashier closed the till and the cash counted was far from what the sales say it should be.

limits.limit: Cash difference above which a closed till is flagged

standalone.branch_sales_low.plain: A branch sold far less than it normally sells on that day of the week.
standalone.branch_sales_low.example: Branch C sold 18,000 on Saturday; a normal Saturday is about 52,000.

standalone.cash_deposit_gap.plain: The cash your tills took is well above the cash that reached the bank.
standalone.cash_deposit_gap.example: Branch A recorded 310,000 cash sales this week but only 255,000 was deposited.

limits.days: How many days of sales to compare
limits.grace_days: Days a deposit may take to reach the bank
limits.tolerance_percent: How big a gap (in %) is allowed before flagging

standalone.sale_without_payment.plain: A sale was recorded as paid by mobile money or bank transfer, but no matching payment shows on the statements.
standalone.sale_without_payment.example: A 4,800 sale says mobile money, and no payment of that code or amount appears around that time.
standalone.sale_without_payment.needs: Sales and payments (statements or an ERP)

limits.days: How many days back to look
limits.grace_hours: Hours to wait for the payment to appear
limits.window_minutes: How many minutes apart a payment and a sale can be and still match
limits.high_count: Number of such sales at which the alert becomes high priority

controls.after_hours_activity.plain: Someone made many changes in the system outside working hours.
controls.after_hours_activity.example: One user made 31 changes between 23:00 and 02:00 on Sunday.

limits.min_actions: Fewest changes before it is flagged

controls.approval_by_requester.plain: Something was approved by the same person who asked for it, so nobody else looked.
controls.approval_by_requester.example: A stock write-off was requested and approved by the same manager.

controls.exceptions_backlog.plain: Problems the system put in its exceptions inbox (things it could not finish by itself) have waited too long for someone to look.
controls.exceptions_backlog.example: 11 items have been waiting for more than 7 days.

limits.days: Days an item may wait before it counts as stuck
limits.min_items: Fewest stuck items before it is flagged

controls.new_wide_access.plain: Someone was recently given a role that lets them act across the whole business or a whole company.
controls.new_wide_access.example: A new user was given the Finance Manager role for all branches on Monday.

crm.duplicate_customers.plain: A customer was created with the same phone number or tax number as an existing one, which can be used to get more credit than one account allows.
crm.duplicate_customers.example: Two accounts share one phone number, each with its own credit limit.

finance.large_manual_journal.plain: A hand-made accounting entry is bigger than the limit you set for such entries.
finance.large_manual_journal.example: A 240,000 manual entry when your limit is 100,000.

limits.limit: Amount above which a hand-made entry is flagged

finance.odd_hours_manual_journal.plain: A hand-made accounting entry was created late at night or very early in the morning.
finance.odd_hours_manual_journal.example: A manual entry was posted at 02:15.

limits.start_hour: Hour the odd period starts (24-hour clock)
limits.end_hour: Hour the odd period ends (24-hour clock)

finance.round_manual_journal.plain: A hand-made accounting entry is a perfectly round amount, which real transactions rarely are.

limits.round_unit: Round figures are multiples of this

finance.same_person_approval.plain: One person both prepared and approved a hand-made entry or an expense.
finance.same_person_approval.example: The same user wrote and approved a 75,000 journal.

inventory.adjustment_spike.plain: One person took far more stock out by hand today (write-offs, corrections) than is normal for them.
inventory.adjustment_spike.example: A storekeeper wrote off 4,200 of stock today; their usual is under 300.

inventory.count_variance.plain: A stock count found a lot more or less than the records said was there.
inventory.count_variance.example: The Branch B count came out 7,900 short.

limits.value_limit: Value of the difference above which a count is flagged

inventory.large_write_down.plain: Stock worth a large amount was written off or corrected downwards by hand.
inventory.large_write_down.example: 3,600 of paint was written off as damaged.

limits.value_limit: Value above which a write-off is flagged

inventory.shrinkage_rate.plain: At a branch, a product is being lost (write-offs, short counts) at a high rate compared with what is sold and received.
inventory.shrinkage_rate.example: Branch A lost 14% of the sugar it handled this month.

limits.percent: Loss rate (in %) above which a product is flagged

inventory.unusual_stock_moves.plain: A stock correction or transfer was made outside working hours, or dated well before it was entered.
inventory.unusual_stock_moves.example: A stock correction made at 23:10 and dated four days earlier.

limits.backdate_days: Days earlier than entry date that counts as back-dated

payments.manual_without_evidence.plain: A large mobile-money, bank or card payment was typed in, but your payment provider has no record of it.
payments.manual_without_evidence.example: A 9,500 mobile-money payment was recorded at the till and the provider shows nothing.

limits.amount_limit: Amount above which a payment needs proof
limits.hours: Hours to wait for the provider's record

payments.missing_close.plain: A branch took money on a day but nobody closed that day.
payments.missing_close.example: Branch B has takings on Wednesday and no daily close.

limits.grace_days: Days a close may be late before it is flagged

payments.possible_duplicates.plain: Two payments of the same amount from the same payer were recorded within minutes of each other.
payments.possible_duplicates.example: Two payments of 2,400 from one phone number, four minutes apart.

limits.window_minutes: How many minutes apart counts as a possible duplicate

payments.reversed_after_match.plain: A payment that had been confirmed and matched to a sale was later undone.
payments.reversed_after_match.example: A 6,000 payment, matched to a sale on Monday, was reversed on Wednesday.

people.changes_before_payroll.plain: Someone was added, had their pay raised, or had their bank or mobile-money details changed shortly before a payroll that paid them.
people.changes_before_payroll.example: A new employee was added two days before payroll and paid in full.

limits.days: Days before a payroll run that count as just before
limits.lookback_days: How far back to look for payroll runs

people.pay_self_approved.plain: A person's pay terms or payment details were approved by the same person who proposed them.
people.pay_self_approved.example: A salary increase was proposed and approved by the same payroll clerk.

pos.cashier_discount_rate.plain: A cashier gave away a much bigger share of the list price in discounts and price changes than they usually do.
pos.cashier_discount_rate.example: Cashier B discounted 9% of what they sold yesterday; their usual is 2%.

limits.days: How many recent days to judge

pos.cashier_refund_rate.plain: A cashier gave back money (refunds) on a much bigger share of their sales than they usually do.
pos.cashier_refund_rate.example: Cashier A refunded 11% of their sales yesterday; their usual is 1%.

limits.days: How many recent days to judge

pos.cashier_void_rate.plain: A cashier cancelled (voided) a much bigger share of their sales than they usually do.
pos.cashier_void_rate.example: Cashier B cancelled 14 sales after 9pm; they usually cancel one or two a day.

limits.days: How many recent days to judge

pos.large_exception.plain: A single sale was cancelled, a single refund was given or a single sale was discounted for a large amount.
pos.large_exception.example: A 6,800 sale was cancelled after payment was taken.

limits.days: How many days back to look

pos.reference_missing.plain: A product marked as needing a reference note at the till (for example a prescription or controlled item) was sold without one.
pos.reference_missing.example: Three controlled items were sold on Tuesday with no reference typed.

limits.days: How many days back to look
limits.high_after: Sales by one cashier before it becomes urgent

pos.late_recorded_sales.plain: A sale was entered, or arrived from an offline till, days after the day it is dated.
pos.late_recorded_sales.example: A sale dated Monday was entered on Friday.

pos.out_of_hours_sales.plain: Sales were made at a branch before it normally opens or after it normally closes.
pos.out_of_hours_sales.example: Four sales were rung up at 01:30 at Branch A.

purchasing.duplicate_supplier_bill.plain: Two bills from the same supplier have the same amount close together, or the same invoice number.
purchasing.duplicate_supplier_bill.example: Two bills of 18,400 from one supplier, entered three days apart.

limits.within_days: How many days apart counts as close together

purchasing.duplicate_supplier_payment.plain: A supplier was paid the same amount twice within a few days, or two payments share a reference.
purchasing.duplicate_supplier_payment.example: Supplier X was paid 18,400 on Monday and again on Wednesday.

limits.within_days: How many days apart counts as close together

purchasing.supplier_bank_changed.plain: A supplier's bank or mobile-money details were replaced recently, a common step in payment fraud.
purchasing.supplier_bank_changed.example: Supplier Y's bank account changed on Thursday, before a payment on Friday.

standalone.cashier_discount_rate.plain: A cashier gave away a much bigger share of the list price in discounts than they usually do.
standalone.cashier_discount_rate.example: Cashier B discounted 9% of what they sold yesterday; their usual is 2%.

limits.days: How many recent days to judge

standalone.cashier_refund_rate.plain: A cashier refunded a much bigger share of what they sold than they usually do.
standalone.cashier_refund_rate.example: Cashier A refunded 11% of their sales yesterday; their usual is 1%.

limits.days: How many recent days to judge

standalone.cashier_void_rate.plain: A cashier cancelled a much bigger share of their sales than they usually do.
standalone.cashier_void_rate.example: Cashier B cancelled 14 sales after 9pm; they usually cancel one or two a day.

limits.days: How many recent days to judge

standalone.large_exception.plain: A single sale was cancelled, refunded or discounted for a large amount.
standalone.large_exception.example: A 6,800 sale was cancelled after payment was taken.
standalone.large_exception.needs: Sales with cancellations, refunds or discounts recorded

limits.days: How many days back to look

standalone.late_entered_sales.plain: A sale was entered into the system days after the day it is dated.
standalone.late_entered_sales.example: A sale dated Monday was entered on Friday.
standalone.late_entered_sales.needs: Sales from a source that records when each entry was made

standalone.out_of_hours_sales.plain: Sales were made at a branch before it normally opens or after it normally closes.
standalone.out_of_hours_sales.example: Four sales were rung up at 01:30 at Branch A.
standalone.out_of_hours_sales.needs: Sales with the time of sale

crm.credit_increase_waiting.plain: A request to raise a customer's credit limit has been waiting for approval too long.
crm.credit_increase_waiting.example: A credit increase for Customer A has waited 9 days.

limits.days: Days a request may wait before it is flagged

crm.followups_overdue.plain: A salesperson has follow-ups with possible customers that are overdue.
crm.followups_overdue.example: A salesperson has 7 follow-ups that are more than 3 days overdue.

limits.days: Days overdue before a follow-up is flagged
limits.many: Number of overdue follow-ups at which it becomes more serious

crm.over_credit_limit.plain: A customer's unpaid invoices, less any money they hold on account, are above their credit limit. Customers with no limit set are not checked.
crm.over_credit_limit.example: Customer B owes 140,000 against a limit of 100,000.

limits.high_over_pct: How far over the limit (in %) makes it high priority
limits.max_customers: Most customers checked in one run

pos.credit_to_overdue_customer.plain: A new credit sale or invoice was made to a customer who already had an overdue invoice unpaid.
pos.credit_to_overdue_customer.example: Customer C received a 22,000 invoice while a 31,000 invoice was 47 days overdue.

limits.days: How many days back to look for new credit sales
limits.grace_days: Days of overdue allowed before it counts

pos.customer_over_credit_limit.plain: A customer owes more than the credit limit set for them.
pos.customer_over_credit_limit.example: Customer B owes 140,000 against a limit of 100,000.

limits.tolerance_percent: How far over the limit (in %) is allowed before flagging
limits.high_percent: How far over the limit (in %) makes it high priority

pos.customer_overdue.plain: A customer has an invoice that is past its due date by more than the number of days you set.
pos.customer_overdue.example: Customer A owes 680,000, and the oldest invoice is 45 days late.

pos.customer_paying_slower.plain: A customer now takes much longer to pay than they used to.
pos.customer_paying_slower.example: Customer D used to pay in 18 days and now takes 41.

limits.window_days: How many days of invoices to compare with the period before

standalone.credit_to_overdue_customer.plain: A new invoice was made out to a customer who already had an overdue invoice unpaid.
standalone.credit_to_overdue_customer.example: Customer C was invoiced 22,000 while a 31,000 invoice was 47 days overdue.

limits.days: How many days back to look for new invoices
limits.grace_days: Days of overdue allowed before it counts

standalone.customer_overdue.plain: A customer has an invoice that is past its due date by more than the number of days you set.
standalone.customer_overdue.example: Customer A owes 680,000, and the oldest invoice is 45 days late.

standalone.customer_paying_slower.plain: A customer now takes much longer to pay than they used to.
standalone.customer_paying_slower.example: Customer D used to pay in 18 days and now takes 41.
standalone.customer_paying_slower.needs: Invoices and payments that name the invoice they pay

limits.window_days: How many days of invoices to compare with the period before

people.leave_waiting.plain: A leave request has waited too long for a decision.
people.leave_waiting.example: A leave request has waited 8 days for approval.

limits.days: Days a request may wait before it is flagged

people.paid_without_attendance.plain: An employee was paid in a payroll run with no attendance and no approved leave for that period, while most others paid in the same run do have records.
people.paid_without_attendance.example: Employee C was paid a full month with no attendance recorded, though 9 of 10 colleagues have it.

limits.usage_pct: Share (in %) of people who must have attendance for this check to apply

people.pay_jump_unexplained.plain: An employee's pay changed by a lot from the last payroll, and nothing recorded (a pay change, overtime, unpaid leave, a part month) explains it.
people.pay_jump_unexplained.example: Employee B's gross pay rose 38% with no recorded reason.

limits.percent: How big a change (in %) is flagged

people.payroll_overdue.plain: A payroll run is still not approved, or approved but not paid, days after its pay date.
people.payroll_overdue.example: Payroll for September was due on the 28th and is still unapproved on the 3rd.

limits.days: Days after the pay date before it is flagged

people.unusual_overtime.plain: Overtime on a recent day is far above what that employee, or their branch, normally works.
people.unusual_overtime.example: Employee A worked 9 hours of overtime on Saturday; their usual is under 2.

limits.recent_days: How many recent days to look at

standalone.new_user.plain: A new user was added to the connected system recently.
standalone.new_user.example: A new user called User X appeared in the ERP on Tuesday.

inventory.batch_expired.plain: A batch of stock is past its expiry date and is still counted as stock.
inventory.batch_expired.example: 40 packs of syrup expired on 1 October and are still on the shelf record.

limits.days_back: How far back to look for expired batches

inventory.batch_expiring.plain: A batch with stock still on hand will expire within the next few weeks.
inventory.batch_expiring.example: 60 units of a medicine expire in 12 days.

limits.urgent_days: Days left at which it becomes more serious

inventory.low_stock.plain: A product's stock at a branch has fallen to its reorder level or below.
inventory.low_stock.example: Branch A has 6 bags of cement left and the reorder level is 10.

inventory.negative_stock.plain: The system shows less than zero of a product at a branch, so a delivery or transfer was probably not recorded.
inventory.negative_stock.example: Branch B shows minus 12 bags of sugar.

inventory.out_of_stock.plain: A product you normally sell at a branch has run out.
inventory.out_of_stock.example: Branch A has no cooking oil, and it sold 40 litres last month.

limits.days: How many days back to look for products you normally sell

inventory.slow_stock.plain: A branch holds a lot of stock that has not sold or moved for months.
inventory.slow_stock.example: Branch C has 14,000 of paint that has not sold in 120 days.

limits.days: Days without a sale before stock counts as slow
limits.min_value: Smallest value of stock worth flagging

inventory.transfer_not_received.plain: Stock sent from one branch to another has been on its way for days without being received.
inventory.transfer_not_received.example: A transfer of 20 cartons left Branch A six days ago and Branch B has not received it.

limits.days: Days in transit before it is flagged

standalone.negative_stock.plain: More of a product went out than ever came in, judged on the stock movements you connected.
standalone.negative_stock.example: Sugar shows minus 30 units, so a delivery or opening count is probably missing.
standalone.negative_stock.needs: Stock movements, including opening stock or history from the start

standalone.shrinkage_by_product.plain: A product has lost a lot of stock to write-offs and short counts over the last weeks.
standalone.shrinkage_by_product.example: Cooking oil lost 85 litres to write-offs and short counts this month.

limits.days: How many days of movements to add up
limits.min_loss: Smallest loss in value worth flagging
limits.min_units: Smallest loss in units worth flagging

standalone.stock_adjustment.plain: Stock was written off or corrected for a large amount, at odd hours, or entered days after its date.
standalone.stock_adjustment.example: A 90,000 stock write-off was entered at 23:50.

limits.min_quantity: Smallest number of units worth flagging

purchasing.bill_mismatch_waiting.plain: A supplier's bill does not match what was ordered or received, and nobody has decided what to do.
purchasing.bill_mismatch_waiting.example: A bill for 50 units, when only 42 were received, has waited 6 days.

limits.waiting_days: Days a mismatch may wait before it is flagged

purchasing.margin_squeeze.plain: A product costs more now, and your selling price has not moved, so little profit is left.
purchasing.margin_squeeze.example: Cement cost rose 17% and the margin fell from 12% to 3%.

limits.cost_rise_percent: How big a cost rise (in %) is flagged
limits.min_margin_percent: Profit margin (in %) below which the squeeze is flagged

purchasing.order_above_usual_price.plain: An open purchase order has a price well above what this supplier charged before.
purchasing.order_above_usual_price.example: An order prices rice at 142 a bag; this supplier's earlier price was 120.

limits.above_percent: How far above the usual price (in %) is flagged

purchasing.overdue_supplier_bills.plain: Supplier bills are still unpaid well after they were due, which can damage trust or bring late fees.
purchasing.overdue_supplier_bills.example: Supplier Z has 3 bills, the oldest 38 days overdue.

limits.overdue_days: Days past the due date before it is flagged
limits.serious_days: Days past the due date at which it becomes serious

purchasing.paid_without_receipt.plain: A paid supplier bill charges for goods that never arrived, were sent back, or arrived short.
purchasing.paid_without_receipt.example: Bill 1043 was paid for 100 units; 80 were received.

purchasing.supplier_price_rise.plain: A supplier's latest price for a product is well above what they charged in earlier deliveries.
purchasing.supplier_price_rise.example: The price of cement rose from 700 to 820 a bag between deliveries.

limits.rise_percent: How big a rise (in %) is flagged

standalone.duplicate_payment.plain: The same amount was paid out twice to the same payee within a short time.
standalone.duplicate_payment.example: 18,400 was paid to Supplier X on Monday and again on Wednesday.

limits.hours_apart: How many hours apart counts as a possible duplicate

standalone.duplicate_supplier_invoice.plain: Two invoices from the same supplier have the same number or amount and nearly the same date.
standalone.duplicate_supplier_invoice.example: Two invoices of 18,400 from Supplier X, two days apart.

limits.lookback_days: How many days back to look
limits.days_apart: How many days apart counts as close

standalone.supplier_price_rise.plain: The latest purchase of a product was at a price well above the average of earlier purchases.
standalone.supplier_price_rise.example: Rice cost 142 a bag in the latest purchase, and 120 on average before.

limits.rise_percent: How big a rise (in %) is flagged

memberships.ending.plain: An active membership is cancelled for the end of its period, or reaches its end date, within the next couple of weeks. A chance to speak to the member before they go.
memberships.ending.example: Gold membership of Amina ends in 9 days and brings in 100.00 a month.

limits.days: How many days ahead to look
limits.max_members: Most memberships checked in one run

memberships.packages_expiring.plain: A session package a customer paid for still has credits left and runs out soon. They lose what they paid for unless they book.
memberships.packages_expiring.example: Package PKG-000012 (10 massages) expires in 6 days with 4 of 10 credits unused.

limits.days: How many days ahead to look
limits.min_credits: Fewest unused credits worth a reminder
limits.max_packages: Most packages checked in one run

memberships.recurring_invoice_failed.plain: A repeating invoice, or a membership renewal, was due but could not be made, often because the customer is over their credit limit. Until it is fixed that customer is not being billed.
memberships.recurring_invoice_failed.example: The invoice for Monthly retainer for the period starting 1 October could not be issued.

limits.high_after_days: Days a failure waits before it becomes high priority
limits.lookback_days: How many days back to look
limits.max_runs: Most invoices checked in one run

memberships.revenue_at_risk.plain: A large share of the money you expect from members each month comes from memberships that are cancelling, on hold, or whose renewal invoice failed.
memberships.revenue_at_risk.example: 6 memberships worth 600.00 a month (30% of membership income) are cancelling, on hold or not being billed.

limits.min_percent: Share of monthly income (in %) at risk before it is shown
limits.high_percent: Share (in %) that makes it high priority
limits.min_members: Fewest memberships at risk before it is shown

memberships.members_inactive.plain: Several paying members have not been in for a few weeks. They are the members who cancel next, so a call this week is worth more than a call after they leave.
memberships.members_inactive.example: 14 paying members have not visited for 3 weeks or more. Together they pay 62,000.00 a month.

limits.idle_weeks: Weeks without a visit before a member counts as gone quiet
limits.min_members: Fewest members needed before it is shown
limits.max_members: Most memberships checked in one run

memberships.payment_late.plain: Membership fees are unpaid past their due date. Late-payment messages go out by themselves; this tells you how much is still out and for how long.
memberships.payment_late.example: 9 members owe 41,500.00 in membership fees. The oldest invoice is 34 days late.

limits.min_days_late: Days late before it is shown
limits.high_days_late: Days late that make it high priority

memberships.entry_overrides.plain: A person at the front desk let in many people the check-in had refused. Now and then is normal; a lot may mean free entry for friends.
memberships.entry_overrides.example: Wanjiru let in 8 people the check-in had refused in the last 7 days.

limits.lookback_days: How many days back to look
limits.max_overrides: Refused people one person may let in before it is flagged

bookings.no_show_rate.plain: Many of the appointments for one staff member or room end with the client not turning up. Each no-show is an hour that earned nothing.
bookings.no_show_rate.example: Chair 2 had 12 appointments in the last 30 days and 4 of them (33%) were no-shows.

limits.lookback_days: How many days back to look
limits.min_appointments: Fewest appointments needed before it is judged
limits.no_show_percent: Share of no-shows (in %) that is flagged

bookings.late_cancellations.plain: Clients are cancelling too close to the appointment for the slot to be filled again.
bookings.late_cancellations.example: 7 appointments at the Westlands branch were cancelled inside the cancellation window in the last 30 days.

limits.lookback_days: How many days back to look
limits.late_cancel_count: How many late cancellations are flagged

bookings.low_utilisation.plain: A staff member or room is booked for only a small part of the hours they work, so paid time is going unused.
bookings.low_utilisation.example: Amina was booked for 10 of her 40 working hours in the last 14 days (25%).

limits.lookback_days: How many days back to look
limits.utilisation_percent: Booked share of working hours (in %) below which it is flagged
limits.min_hours: Fewest working hours needed before it is judged

bookings.double_booking_refused.plain: Many booking attempts were refused because the time was already taken. People want those times, so you may need more capacity or longer hours.
bookings.double_booking_refused.example: 9 bookings were refused in the last 7 days because the time was already taken.

limits.lookback_days: How many days back to look
limits.refused_count: How many refused bookings are flagged

bookings.idle_gaps.plain: A staff member has a long empty stretch between two appointments on a coming day, which could be filled or used for time off.
bookings.idle_gaps.example: Joseph has a 3 hour gap between his 10:00 and 14:00 appointments on Thursday.

limits.look_ahead_days: How many days ahead to look
limits.gap_minutes: Length of gap (in minutes) that is flagged
limits.max_findings: Most gaps shown in one run

bookings.completed_not_invoiced.plain: Appointments finished several days ago, with a client and a price, still have no invoice. Only checked when Point of Sale is on.
bookings.completed_not_invoiced.example: 3 appointments finished last week for a total of 12,000 have no invoice.

limits.invoice_after_days: Days after the appointment before it should have an invoice
limits.lookback_days: How many days back to look

jobs.stuck_in_stage.plain: A job has stayed in the same stage for a long time without moving, so a customer may be waiting for nothing.
jobs.stuck_in_stage.example: Job 1042 has been In repair for 19 days.

limits.open_days: Days in an active stage before it is flagged
limits.waiting_days: Days in a waiting stage before it is flagged
limits.serious_days: Days after which it is high priority

jobs.estimate_not_approved.plain: A customer has had an estimate for days and has neither approved nor declined it. The work cannot start until they answer.
jobs.estimate_not_approved.example: The estimate for job 1051 was sent 8 days ago and nobody has answered.

limits.waiting_days: Days an estimate waits before it is flagged

jobs.parts_not_invoiced.plain: A job was collected or closed with parts and labour on it, but no invoice was made, so the work is unpaid.
jobs.parts_not_invoiced.example: Job 1033 was collected 5 days ago with 8,500 of parts and labour and has no invoice.

limits.grace_days: Days allowed before an invoice is expected
limits.look_back_days: How many days back to look

jobs.repeat_returns.plain: Several return visits inside the warranty trace back to the same person's work, which may mean a training or quality problem.
jobs.repeat_returns.example: Peter's work came back 4 times in 90 days under warranty.

limits.min_returns: Fewest return visits that are flagged
limits.look_back_days: How many days back to look

jobs.ready_not_collected.plain: A finished job has been waiting for the customer to collect it for many days. It takes up space and the customer may have forgotten.
jobs.ready_not_collected.example: A phone repair has been ready for collection for 12 days.

limits.waiting_days: Days waiting before it is flagged
limits.serious_days: Days after which it is high priority

timebilling.unbilled_ageing.plain: Approved time and expenses for a client have been waiting a long while for an invoice. Work done but not billed is money not collected.
timebilling.unbilled_ageing.example: Client Acme has 18,000 of approved time that is 45 days old and not invoiced.

limits.unbilled_days: Days waiting before it is flagged
limits.look_back_days: How many days back to look

timebilling.project_over_budget.plain: A project has used more hours or money than its budget, so it is losing money unless the client agrees to more.
timebilling.project_over_budget.example: Website redesign has used 120 of its 100 budgeted hours (120%).

limits.over_percent: Share of budget used (in %) that is flagged

timebilling.timesheets_not_submitted.plain: Someone logged time for a week that has ended but has not sent it in for approval, so it cannot be billed.
timebilling.timesheets_not_submitted.example: Grace logged 32 hours in the week of 6 October and has not submitted them.

limits.grace_days: Days after the week ends before it is flagged
limits.look_back_weeks: How many weeks back to look

timebilling.approval_waiting.plain: A submitted week has been waiting a long while for someone to approve it, which holds up invoicing.
timebilling.approval_waiting.example: David's timesheet for the week of 6 October has waited 6 days for approval.

limits.approval_days: Days waiting before it is flagged
limits.look_back_days: How many days back to look

timebilling.retainer_nearly_used.plain: A client's prepaid hours are almost all used, or are about to expire unused. Time to talk about a top-up or to use the hours.
timebilling.retainer_nearly_used.example: Acme has used 42 of its 50 retainer hours (84%).

limits.used_percent: Share of prepaid hours used (in %) that is flagged

timebilling.billable_ratio_drop.plain: The share of logged hours that can be billed has dropped well below the weeks before, so more time is going on work nobody pays for.
timebilling.billable_ratio_drop.example: Billable share fell from 72% to 55% over the last 14 days.

limits.share_drop_points: Fall in billable share (in points) that is flagged
limits.min_logged_hours: Fewest logged hours needed before it is judged

claims.estimate_waiting.plain: A payer has had an estimate for days and has not answered every line.
claims.estimate_waiting.example: The estimate for claim CLM-HQ-000012 has waited 8 days for the insurer's answer.

claims.approved_not_started.plain: The payer approved the work days ago and the job has not started.
claims.approved_not_started.example: Claim CLM-HQ-000015 was approved 4 days ago and the car has not been touched.

claims.counter_unanswered.plain: A payer offered less for a line and nobody has accepted or argued it.
claims.counter_unanswered.example: The insurer offered 1,500 less on claim CLM-HQ-000009 five days ago.

claims.supplementary_not_sent.plain: Extra work was written up and never sent to the payer.
claims.supplementary_not_sent.example: Extra work of 2,500 on claim CLM-HQ-000020 has sat as a draft for 3 days.

claims.completed_not_invoiced.plain: Work was signed off as done and the claim has no invoice.
claims.completed_not_invoiced.example: Claim CLM-HQ-000003 was signed off 6 days ago and is worth 19,750 with no invoice.

limits.look_back_days: How many days back to look

claims.payer_invoice_overdue.plain: A payer's invoice is past its due date and still unpaid.
claims.payer_invoice_overdue.example: The insurer owes 17,250 on an invoice 40 days past due.

limits.late_days: Days past due before it is flagged
limits.look_back_days: How many days back to look

claims.payer_rejects_more.plain: One payer rejects a much larger share of the money asked than your other payers.
claims.payer_rejects_more.example: One insurer rejected 38% of the money asked, your others 12%.

limits.times_usual: How many times more than your other payers
limits.look_back_days: How many days back to look
limits.min_lines: Fewest answered lines before a payer is compared

claims.rejection_reasons_repeat.plain: A payer keeps giving the same reason for rejecting lines.
claims.rejection_reasons_repeat.example: An insurer rejected paint 5 times with the reason 'not covered'.

limits.min_repeats: How many times the same reason counts
limits.look_back_days: How many days back to look

claims.short_pay_open.plain: A payer paid less than invoiced and the difference is still open.
claims.short_pay_open.example: An insurer paid 696 less than invoiced 16 days ago.

bookings.deposits_unpaid.plain: Appointments that need a deposit are coming up and the deposit has not been paid. These are the bookings most likely to be missed.
bookings.deposits_unpaid.example: 4 appointments in the next 3 days still have an unpaid deposit.

limits.min_count: Fewest unpaid deposits before it is flagged
limits.look_ahead_days: How many days ahead to look

bookings.tips_held.plain: Tips taken by card or mobile money are still held by the business after several days. They belong to the staff and should be handed over.
bookings.tips_held.example: KES 6,400 in tips has been held for 9 days.

limits.older_than_days: How many days a tip may be held before it is flagged
limits.min_amount: Smallest total (in money) that is flagged

jobs.courtesy_car_overdue.plain: A courtesy car lent to a customer has not come back by the date it was due. The car is out of use and cannot be lent to the next customer.
jobs.courtesy_car_overdue.example: The courtesy car lent on the 3rd was due back 5 days ago.

limits.late_days: How many days late before it is flagged

jobs.part_overdue.plain: A part ordered for a repair has not arrived by its expected date. The vehicle takes up a bay and the customer is waiting.
jobs.part_overdue.example: The brake pads ordered for a repair are 3 days past their expected date.

limits.late_days: How many days late before it is flagged

timebilling.realisation_low.plain: Recently invoiced work was billed for much less than it was worth because hours were written down or off. The business pays for that time, not the client.
timebilling.realisation_low.example: Of 240,000 of work invoiced in the last 60 days, only 168,000 (70%) was billed.

limits.min_percent: Share of the work's value (in %) that should be billed
limits.look_back_days: How many days back to look
limits.min_value: Smallest amount of work that is judged

timebilling.review_waiting.plain: An invoice is held until a partner approves it and has been waiting for days. The client cannot be billed until someone looks at it.
timebilling.review_waiting.example: An invoice for a client has waited 5 days for a partner to approve it.

limits.waiting_days: How many days it may wait before it is flagged

timebilling.work_overdue.plain: Dated client work, such as a filing or a monthly close, is still open after its due date. Late work costs trust, and the fee cannot be billed until it is done.
timebilling.work_overdue.example: The monthly bookkeeping for a client is still open 6 days after its due date.

limits.grace_days: How many days after the due date before it is flagged

bookings.class_underfilled.plain: A class or lesson in the next few days has only a few of its places taken, so the teacher and room are used for very little fee income.
bookings.class_underfilled.example: Maths Form 2 on Tuesday at 16:00 has 2 of 12 places taken (17%).

limits.look_ahead_days: How many days ahead to look
limits.fill_percent: Share of places taken (in %) below which a class is flagged
limits.max_sessions: Most classes to show at once

bookings.class_absences.plain: A learner or member has been marked absent from several classes in the last weeks. It is often the first sign a family is about to stop.
bookings.class_absences.example: Grace was absent from 4 sessions in the last 28 days.

limits.lookback_days: How many days back to look
limits.absences: Number of absences before a person is flagged
limits.high_count: Number of absences at which it becomes urgent
limits.max_people: Most people to show at once

memberships.term_ending_unpaid.plain: A term, course or contract is about to end while some invoices on it are still unpaid. After it ends, those fees are much harder to collect.
memberships.term_ending_unpaid.example: 6 families still owe KES 48,000 on terms that end within 14 days.

limits.look_ahead_days: How many days ahead to look
limits.min_amount: Smallest total owed that is flagged
